standard_prerequisites.name: Regularity on a quotient by the previous elements

standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces a transposition in the middle of the sequence to the two-term case over a quotient module.

core_obligations: Case c = 2: show multiplication by x_1 on the kernel K of x_2 is surjective using that x_2 is a nonzerodivisor modulo x_1, and conclude K = 0 by Nakayama (proof lines 16865-16872).
Still in case c = 2: compute the kernel of multiplication by x_1 on M/x_2M and use regularity of the pair to show it vanishes (proof lines 16873-16878).
General case: every permutation is a product of adjacent transpositions, and the two-term case applied to the quotient by the earlier elements handles one transposition (proof lines 16880-16889).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to swapping two consecutive terms and treat that case directly (proof lines 16864-16878).
Assemble the general permutation from adjacent transpositions on quotients (proof lines 16880-16890).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a local Noetherian ring and a finite module, any permutation of a regular sequence is again regular (statement lines 16855-16862). The proof does not use the Koszul complex or a dimension count: it treats the case of two elements directly by analysing the kernel of multiplication by the second element and concluding by Nakayama, then handles the general case by writing a permutation as a product of adjacent transpositions and applying the two-element case to the quotient by the preceding elements (proof lines 16864-16890). The reduction to adjacent transpositions on a quotient is what makes the general case follow from the two-term one. H2.
